theory.intro: A **similarity statement** names two similar figures with their vertices in **matching order**, joined by $\sim$, e.g. $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle LMK$. The order records which vertices correspond, so matching angles and sides can be read straight off the letters.
facts: $\sim$ means "is similar to": $ABCD \sim EFGH$ says the two quadrilaterals are similar.
In $ABCD \sim EFGH$ the vertices are in matching order, so $\angle ABC = \angle EFG$ and side $AB$ corresponds to side $EF$.

Find corresponding vertices using equal angles, corresponding side relationships and the order around each figure, not positions on the page. Repeated equal angles alone may not identify matching vertices; a rotated or reflected figure changes nothing.
A statement with the letters out of matching order is wrong, even when the figures really are similar.
steps: Identify the corresponding vertices using equal angles, corresponding side relationships and the order around each figure. When angles repeat, use the sides and boundary order to distinguish the vertices.
Write the vertices of both figures in matching order.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The right angles match $A\leftrightarrow D$, and the $60^{\circ}$ angles match $C\leftrightarrow E$. The remaining vertices match $B\leftrightarrow F$.
$\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE$
The corresponding sides are $AB$ and $DF$, $BC$ and $FE$, and $CA$ and $ED$.
$\angle BCA$ corresponds to $\angle FED$.

The single arcs match $J\leftrightarrow R$, and the double arcs match $K\leftrightarrow S$. The remaining vertices match $L\leftrightarrow T$.
$\triangle JKL\sim\triangle RST$
Side $JK$ corresponds to side $RS$.

Match the endpoints of the sloping sides: $A\leftrightarrow P$ and $B\leftrightarrow Q$. Follow the adjacent sides around each boundary: $C\leftrightarrow R$, $D\leftrightarrow S$, $E\leftrightarrow T$.
$ABCDE\sim PQRST$
Side $CD$ corresponds to side $RS$.
$\angle EAB$ corresponds to $\angle TPQ$.
Matching sides and boundary order distinguish the vertices even where angles repeat.

Consider the two triangles separately.
$\angle KOL=\angle POQ$ (vertically opposite angles).
$\angle OKL=\angle OPQ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).
Thus $K\leftrightarrow P$, $O\leftrightarrow O$ and $L\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\triangle KOL\sim\triangle POQ$
The corresponding sides are $KO$ and $PO$, $OL$ and $OQ$, and $KL$ and $PQ$.

The angle at $D$ is shared.
$\angle DGH=\angle DEF$ and $\angle DHG=\angle DFE$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).
The vertices match $D\leftrightarrow D$, $G\leftrightarrow E$ and $H\leftrightarrow F$.
$\triangle DGH\sim\triangle DEF$
Side $GH$ corresponds to side $EF$.

foundation.solution_text:
$\angle A=\angle L=70^{\circ}$
$\angle B=\angle M=60^{\circ}$
$\angle C=\angle K=50^{\circ}$
$\therefore \triangle ABC \sim \triangle LMK$

Matching the equal angles and corresponding sides around each figure: $A\leftrightarrow L$, $B\leftrightarrow M$, $C\leftrightarrow N$, $D\leftrightarrow P$, $E\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\therefore ABCDE \sim LMNPQ$

Matching the corresponding sides around the figures gives $J\leftrightarrow R$ and $K\leftrightarrow S$.
Side $JK$ corresponds to side $RS$.

The right angles match $D\leftrightarrow S$, and the marked angles match $F\leftrightarrow U$, so $E\leftrightarrow T$.
$\angle EFD$ corresponds to $\angle TUS$.

The single arcs show $\angle P=\angle X$ and the double arcs show $\angle Q=\angle Y$, so the remaining angles give $\angle R=\angle Z$.
A reflected enlargement preserves angles, so the vertices still match by equal angles.
$\therefore \triangle PQR \sim \triangle XYZ$

The obtuse corners match $R\leftrightarrow Y$. Matching the adjacent sides gives $Q\leftrightarrow X$ and $S\leftrightarrow Z$.
$\angle QRS$ corresponds to $\angle XYZ$.

The right angles match $A\leftrightarrow F$, and the marked angles match $C\leftrightarrow H$, so $B\leftrightarrow G$.
$AB$ corresponds to $FG$
$BC$ corresponds to $GH$
$CA$ corresponds to $HF$

development.solution_text:
$\angle A$ is shared by both triangles.
$\angle ADE=\angle ABC$, corresponding angles on parallel lines
$\angle AED=\angle ACB$, corresponding angles on parallel lines
$\therefore \triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$

$\angle KAL=\angle MAN$, vertically opposite angles
$\angle AKL=\angle AMN$, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\angle ALK=\angle ANM$, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\therefore \triangle KAL \sim \triangle MAN$

The acute corners match $B\leftrightarrow S$ and the obtuse corners match $C\leftrightarrow P$. Matching the adjacent sides and following the boundary gives $A\leftrightarrow R$ and $D\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\therefore ABCD \sim RSPQ$

The apex angles correspond, so $M\leftrightarrow P$; following the boundary from there matches $N\leftrightarrow Q$, $J\leftrightarrow R$, $K\leftrightarrow S$, $L\leftrightarrow T$.
$\therefore JKLMN \sim RSTPQ$

The long arm of the first L runs $A$ to $B$, and the matching long arm of the second runs $R$ to $S$, so $A\leftrightarrow R$ and $B\leftrightarrow S$; following the boundary matches $C\leftrightarrow T$, $D\leftrightarrow U$, $E\leftrightarrow P$, $F\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\therefore ABCDEF \sim RSTUPQ$

Matching the sloping sides gives $A\leftrightarrow V$ and $B\leftrightarrow W$. Matching the adjacent sides and following the boundary gives $C\leftrightarrow X$, $D\leftrightarrow Y$ and $E\leftrightarrow Z$.
$\therefore ABCDE \sim VWXYZ$

practice.masteryOmitted: Vertex-order naming is a single-step convention; the hardest honest in-skill cases (overlapping, reflected and rotated figures) already sit in development, and any further twist crosses into similarity testing or unknown-side work owned by sibling skills.
